# Image Enhancement and Restoration Methods
## Overview
Image Enhancement and Restoration Methods address input data degradation in NeRF training by modeling blur, transient occlusions, or missing geometry, enabling sharp novel view synthesis from uncontrolled inputs. [G] Unlike sibling methods that modify internal neural field capacity, these approaches explicitly model the imaging process or separate static components from transient artifacts using external 2D priors and inpainting networks. [G]
## Shared principles
Builds on [Model Architecture Modifications](11313-model-architecture-modifications.md). [G]
## Subtopics

### [DeblurNeRF](11964-deblurnerf.md)
Reconstructs a sharp NeRF from blurry inputs by jointly optimizing a Deformable Sparse Kernel (DSK) module to simulate spatially varying blur. [G] It sets itself apart by using pixel-wise independent deformable kernels rather than global scene priors. [G] Choose this method when computational efficiency is prioritized over strict 3D geometric consistency. [G]

### [IE-NeRF](13737-ie-nerf.md)
Synthesizes novel views in uncontrolled environments by separating static scene properties from transient occlusions using a learned 2D transient mask and a pre-trained inpainting module. [G] It sets itself apart by predicting the mask end-to-end within a single MLP rather than relying on pre-trained semantic segmentation or 3D transient fields. [G] Choose this method for static scene reconstruction in the presence of dynamic elements. [G]

### [Sharp-NeRF](14270-sharp-nerf.md)
Renders clean images from blurry inputs by modeling spatially varying blur using discrete learnable kernels and a precomputed sharpness map. [G] It sets itself apart by replacing neural kernel generators with fixed discrete kernels, significantly reducing training time. [G] Choose this method when fast training with high-quality deblurring is required. [G]

### SPIn-NeRF
A 3D inpainting method that leverages LaMa for color and depth inpainting, replacing pixel loss with perceptual loss for visual coherence and using depth inpainting to supervise 3D geometry. [S1] It sets itself apart by using perceptual loss instead of pixel loss to guide NeRF training. [S1] Choose this method when visual coherence is prioritized over strict pixel-level accuracy. [S1]

## Background
The family originated from efforts to handle low-quality or uncontrolled input data in NeRF training. [G] Early approaches like NeRF-In trained NeRFs with pixel reconstruction loss guided by 2D inpainted images. [S1] SPIn-NeRF improved upon this by leveraging LaMa for color and depth inpainting, replacing pixel loss with perceptual loss for better visual coherence, and using depth inpainting to supervise 3D geometry. [S1] Subsequent methods like Removing-NeRF incorporated posed RGB-D images with 2D masks and confidence-based view selection. [S1] Reference-guided inpainting combined monocular depth estimation with bilateral solvers for view-dependent consistency. [S1] These techniques are primarily used in novel view synthesis pipelines where input images contain blur, transient occlusions, or missing geometry. [G]
